statement: For tsp_guided_insertion_2opt on dev_24, a cost-delta-driven insertion score weighted by candidate-list regret (i.e., favouring cities whose cheapest AND second-cheapest insertion positions are far apart) followed by exhaustive 2-opt to local optimality yields better tour length than plain cheapest-insertion plus fixed-pass 2-opt, because regret-weighted seeding avoids early long-edge locking.
rationale: Empty archive (solver_count=0) and no KB entries specific to the hook; the guided-insertion template exposes score_insertion_move, so the only levers are the insertion scoring function and the 2-opt intensification schedule. Regret-style scoring is the standard literature remedy for greedy insertion's myopia.

statement: For tsp_guided_insertion_2opt on dev_24, a cost-delta-driven insertion score weighted by candidate-list regret (i.e., favouring cities whose cheapest AND second-cheapest insertion positions are far apart) followed by exhaustive 2-opt to local optimality yields better tour length than plain cheapest-insertion plus fixed-pass 2-opt, because regret-weighted seeding avoids early long-edge locking.
rationale: Round 1 baseline established on dev_24: the evolved hook is a two-term blend score = 0.65*normalize(min distance to current tour) + 0.35*(1 - normalize(insertion cost)), i.e. the max-normalisation implicitly couples the two criteria per call. Mean tour length 84687.24 over 36/36 feasible instances at 7.04 ms mean (well inside the 500 ms budget, ~1.4% utilisation), so there is large unused compute headroom that pure hook scoring cannot spend; intensification (2-opt schedule) is the untapped lever. The regret/candidate-list-distance claim itself is not yet isolated, since the reference hook only uses per-city min distance and min insertion cost, not second-best insertion regret.
